# Automatic differentiation is a testing problem

## Nobody can tell you which backend to use

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
| Backend | `Censored` | `Composed` |
|---|---|---|
| ForwardDiff | green | red |
| ReverseDiff, tape | green | red |
| Mooncake forward | green | red |
| Mooncake reverse | green | red |
| Enzyme forward | green, 1 broken | red |
| Enzyme reverse | green, 1 broken | red |

- Each configuration gets its own job, its own badge and its own Codecov
  flag. Both declared broken scenarios are the same `convolve_series`
  case on a stacked `IntervalCensored{Truncated{PrimaryCensored}}`
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- DifferentiationInterface tells you about a function. Turing tells you
  what Turing tests. Nothing tells you about a model assembled from five
  packages that each tested on their own
- The one public per-backend table for a probabilistic programming
  stack, `TuringLang/ADTests`, was archived in June

::: {.attribution}
`Censored` is `CensoredDistributions.jl`, `Composed` is
`ComposedDistributions.jl` · declared broken scenarios in
[CensoredDistributions.jl#889][cd889], read from `test/ADFixtures` on
`main` · last `AD` run on `main` green 2026-06-21 there and red on all
six 2026-08-07 in `ComposedDistributions.jl` ·
[TuringLang/ADTests][adtests], archived 2026-06-15.
:::
:::
::::

## What we added on top of DifferentiationInterfaceTest

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- DifferentiationInterfaceTest works per function and per package. We
  added a registry where a package declares which scenarios are broken
  on which backend, and `check_broken` re-runs them
- `gamma_inc` and `beta_inc` carry no AD rules, so we hand-wrote those
  derivatives. `ScoringRules.jl` hit the same two from scratch
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fanout}
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  L["One declared list<br>of backends and<br>broken scenarios"]
  M["Six CI jobs"]
  F["Six Codecov flags"]
  B["Six README badges"]
  T["One published<br>support table"]
  L --> M
  L --> F
  L --> B
  L --> T
```
:::

::: {.attribution}
Schematic of what the list feeds, drawn for this talk. The list is
`_AD_BACKENDS` in `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl`, `src/scaffold.jl:1464`.
Its six entries are what the managed `.github/workflows/ad.yaml` passes
as its matrix and what the six per backend Codecov badges in each README
point at, read 2026-08-11.
:::
:::
::::

## A wrong number, not an error

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```julia
f(x) = xlogy(x[1], 0.8)   # d/dx = log(0.8)

DI.gradient(f, DI.AutoForwardDiff(), [0.0])
DI.gradient(f, DI.AutoMooncake(), [0.0])
```

| Backend | Gradient at `x = 0` |
|---|---|
| Finite differences | -0.22314 |
| ForwardDiff | -0.22314 |
| ReverseDiff | -0.22314 |
| Enzyme | -0.22314 |
| Mooncake | **0.0** |
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- `logpdf(Gamma(k, θ), x)` computes `xlogy(k - 1, x / θ)`. Mooncake has
  no rule for `xlogy`, so it differentiates the implementation. At shape
  exactly 1.0 the first argument is zero, the `iszero` branch returns a
  constant, and the shape gradient comes back as zero
- Nothing throws. The sampler runs. The number is wrong
- We found it in a pooled model and reduced it to three lines. Our bot
  filed it upstream by mistake and we withdrew it. It is still not
  reported

::: {.callout-important}
`EpiAwareADTools.jl` carries the rule, and deletes it the day Mooncake
ships one.
:::

::: {.attribution}
The three lines and the backend comparison are from
[ComposedDistributions.jl#99][cd99], 2026-07-07. `xlogy` comes from
`LogExpFunctions`, `DI` is `DifferentiationInterface`. Mooncake 0.5.37,
Julia 1.12 · the withdrawn upstream report is
[chalk-lab/Mooncake.jl#1241][mc1241], closed the day it was opened, and
nothing has replaced it as of 2026-08-11 · the local rule is
`ext/EpiAwareADToolsLogExpFunctionsMooncakeExt.jl`.
:::
